import pandas as pd
df=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
d=df[df.account_id=='S5Tfd67'].copy();d['date']=pd.to_datetime(d.date,format='%m/%d/%y')

    print(p.loc['2025-10-10':'2025-10-19'].round(0).to_string())

import pandas as pd
df=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
d=df[df.account_id=='S5Tfd67'].copy();d['date']=pd.to_datetime(d.date,format='%m/%d/%y')
print(d.groupby('date').unblended_cost.sum().loc['2025-10-05':'2025-10-20'])
x=d[(d.cloud_service=='caGYw')&(d.application=='kt5')]
p=x.pivot_table(index='date',columns='instance_family',values='unblended_cost',aggfunc='sum').loc['2025-10-09':'2025-10-19']
print(p.round(0).T.to_string())
print(x[x.date.between('2025-10-11','2025-10-18')].sort_values('date').to_string())

- **What changed:** this instance family usually costs about $77–86 a day. On 10-11 and 10-12 it ran 0 instances and cost nothing. From 10-13 through 10-17 it jumped to 18 instances at $0.40 each, or **$172.80 a day**, which includes the anomaly date of 10-16. On 10-18 it fell back to 1 instance ($9.60), and on 10-19 to $0.
- **Effect higher up:** this is what pushed up the totals for application kt5 (about $170–190 a day normally, $347–360 during this period) and cloud service caGYw (about $350–460 normally, $531–568 during this period). Those two are only listed because they contain this instance family; they are not separate causes.
- **Other resources:** the other instance families under caGYw/kt5 stayed within their normal daily ranges.
- **Account total:** the jump is small at account level. The total on 10-16 was $6,269, within the $6,022–6,321 range seen from 10-05 to 10-20. The anomaly stands out clearly only when you look at the individual resources.
